resume: The Amiga does not generate its sounds, it plays them: Paula reads samples in Chip RAM on 4 stereo channels. You set the period of a note and its volume, start and stop a channel, then rely on Paula's interrupt requests to chain sounds or play a sound effect only once. Tick 🔊 under the screen and start "🎬 Real time" to listen.

amiga-ch09-n2.titre: Chaining sounds, and playing only once

amiga-ch09-rappel.introduction: Three questions on the previous chapters, without rereading the lessons. Getting it wrong here does not matter: searching is what makes it stick.

q1.enonce: D1 receives the first control word of a sprite placed at x = 40, y = 16. What is it?
q1.explication: VSTART = $2C + 16 = $3C goes in the high byte, and HSTART = $81 + 40 = $A9, divided by 2, gives $54.

q2.enonce: After `BTST #7,$BFE001`, the Z flag is 1. What happened?
choix: The left mouse button is pressed
q2.explication: The buttons are active low: Z = 1 means that bit 7, the joystick one, is 0.

choix: It turns on the sprite DMA
It turns off the sprite DMA, without touching the other channels
It turns off all channels except the sprites
q3.explication: Bit 15 of DMACON is 0: the bits at 1 in the word, here SPREN, go to 0, and the others do not move.

amiga-ch09-cours-paula.source: Written for 68k Trainer from the Hardware Reference Manual (ch. 5) and Amiga Intern (Abacus, ch. 11)

amiga-ch09-ex-la.introduction: A 32-byte square wave is played at 440 Hz for 50 frames. Tick 🔊, start "🎬 Real time" and listen; "Vectors and hardware" shows AUD0EN in DMACON.

explications.3: AUD0LC receives the address of the wave, stored in Chip RAM by `SECTION son,DATA_C`, because Paula only reads Chip RAM.
explications.4: AUD0LEN is counted in words: 32 bytes make 16 words.
explications.5: With this period, Paula sends a byte every 252 ticks of its 3.55 MHz clock.
explications.7: DMACON receives SET + DMAEN + AUD0EN, and channel 0 plays the wave in a loop.
explications.11: With bit 15 at 0, AUD0EN goes back to 0: silence.

amiga-ch09-ex-la.conclusion: A held note is a short wave that the DMA replays in a loop, without the 68000 having anything to do while it sounds.

amiga-ch09-pred-periode.introduction: The 68000 computes the period of an A at 440 Hz for a 32-byte wave.

q1.explication: 3,546,895 ÷ 14,080 = 251.9…, and DIVU keeps only the integer part, 251. To round, you add half the divisor before dividing, which gives 252.

q2.enonce: For the same wave, what is the period of an A one octave higher (880 Hz)?
q2.explication: To double the frequency, Paula must send the bytes twice as fast: the period is divided by two, and stays above the minimum of 124.

amiga-ch09-exo-volume.enonce: The program starts an A that you cannot hear, because the volume is at 0: set it to the maximum.

amiga-ch09-exo-ordonner.enonce: Put the lines back in order to compute the period of an A (440 Hz, 32-byte wave), rounded to the nearest integer, and store it in AUD0PER: it must be 252.
indices: To round, you add half the divisor to the clock before dividing.
The divisor, f × N, must be known before you take half of it; the quotient of `DIVU` is in the low word of D0, which `MOVE.W` stores in AUD0PER.

amiga-ch09-exo-octave.enonce: This is the program from the example, which plays an A at 440 Hz at maximum volume. Change it to play the A one octave higher, at 880 Hz, at half the maximum volume.
indices: Doubling the frequency means dividing the period by two. The volume ranges from 0 to 64.

amiga-ch09-exo-muet.titre: The channel that does not start
amiga-ch09-exo-muet.enonce: The program starts channel 0 and waits until Paula has started it, but it waits forever, and the screen goes black. Find the error in the write to DMACON.
indices: What is bit 15 of `$0201`? What does DMACON do with the bits at 1 when it is 0?
`$8201`: SET + DMAEN + AUD0EN. (`$0201` turned off DMAEN, and therefore the screen too.)

amiga-ch09-exo-notes.enonce: Play C (period 423), E (336) then G (283) on channel 0, half a second each (25 frames), then stop the channel.
indices: Start the channel once (LC, LEN, VOL, the period of C, DMACON); to change the note, write only a new period.
A table `DC.W 423,336,283` and `MOVE.W (A0)+,$A6(A5)`; 25 `attendre_vbl` per note; `MOVE.W #$0001,$96(A5)` at the end.

amiga-ch09-cours-enchainer.titre: Paula's requests, the one-shot sound, the filter
amiga-ch09-cours-enchainer.source: Written for 68k Trainer from the Hardware Reference Manual (ch. 5) and the music players (RamJam)

amiga-ch09-ex-unefois.introduction: A 1600-byte beep played once: as soon as Paula has noted the block, you give it a one-word block of silence for what follows.

explications.7: You clear any old AUD0 request (bit 7 of INTREQ, bit 15 at 0).
explications.8: The channel starts: Paula copies LC and LEN into its counters and immediately requests the AUD0 interrupt.
explications.10: Bit 7 of INTREQR (low byte at `$DFF01F`) signals the request: Paula is playing the beep.
explications.12: The next block is only one word of zeros, which Paula will replay in a loop at the end of the beep: silence.
explications.17: You stop the channel whenever you like, since nothing has been heard for a long time.

amiga-ch09-ex-unefois.conclusion: Paula always takes the next block from AUDxLC and AUDxLEN: by changing them as soon as it makes its request, you chain sounds without a gap, or silence it after a single pass.

amiga-ch09-exo-silence.enonce: The beep must be played only once, but the length of the "silence block" is wrong: after the beep, Paula plays 800 words of whatever follows the silence in memory. Fix it.
indices: The silence block is only one word long.

amiga-ch09-exo-demande.enonce: This program must play the beep only once, but it never ends. Step through it while watching INTREQ in "Vectors and hardware": the AUD0 request arrives, and yet the loop goes on. Fix the error.
indices: `BTST` on memory tests only one byte. In which byte of the INTREQR word is bit 7?
The 68000 stores the high byte of a word at the even address: bit 7 of INTREQR is bit 7 of the low byte, at `$DFF01F`. `BTST #7,$1F(A5)`.

amiga-ch09-bonus-stereo.enonce: Challenge: an A (period 252) on channel 0, on the left, and an E (period 336) on channel 1, on the right, started together. Wait until Paula has started both channels (bits 7 and 8 of INTREQR), put 3 in D7, then stop both channels.
indices: The registers of channel 1 are 16 bytes after those of channel 0: `$B0`, `$B4`, `$B6`, `$B8`.
DMACON = `$8203`; then read INTREQR (`$1E(A5)`), keep `$0180` and compare.

q1.enonce: How many channels does Paula have?
q1.explication: Channels 0 and 3 on the left, 1 and 2 on the right.

q2.enonce: A sample is a sequence of bytes that are…
q2.explication: −128 to +127, and Paula only reads Chip RAM.

q3.explication: Paula reads one word (two bytes) at a time.

choix: It turns on all the DMA channels
It turns off all the DMA channels
q9.explication: Bit 15 is 0: all the bits at 1 in the word go to 0 in DMACON.

q4.enonce: The larger the period, the note is…
q4.explication: Paula reads the bytes more slowly, and the frequency drops.

q10.enonce: After a `DIVU`, where is the quotient?
choix: In the high word of the destination
In the low word of the destination
q10.explication: The quotient goes in the low word, and the remainder in the high word.

q7.enonce: When does Paula request a channel's interrupt?
choix: When it has copied LC and LEN, at the start of each block
At the end of the program
q7.explication: It is the signal to prepare the next block.

q8.enonce: How do you play a sound effect only once?
choix: As soon as Paula makes its request, give it a one-word next block of silence
Turn off the DMA right away
q8.explication: The channel will replay the silence in a loop, without a sound.
